title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #1
body: His job title is SMM and his actual job is everything. He shoots, he edits, he writes, he answers the DMs, he argues with the client about the logo size, and he does all of it for one salary. Ask what he charges. If it's per post, he's new. If it's a monthly retainer, he's learned. If he stopped answering the phone after 7pm, he's fully evolved. It's a sealed deal if he has CapCut and Premiere both open on a laptop with 4 GB of RAM.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 every SMM in Baku just felt this.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #2
body: Ask who the client is. Restaurant, beauty salon, dental clinic, or a construction company, that is the entire Baku market and every marketing person cycles through all four. The restaurant wants viral. The salon wants the owner in every frame. The clinic wants before-and-afters that cannot legally be posted. The construction company wants a drone shot of an empty field. It's a sealed deal if a client has ever said "make it like that one that got a million views."
caption:
Tip #2 😭 every SMM in Baku just felt this.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #3
body: Watch the shoot locations. Boulevard at golden hour, Icherisheher for anything traditional, Port Baku for anything premium, Highland Park for anything with a view, and the Flame Towers in the background of all of them. There are six locations in this city and everyone uses the same six. If he's found a seventh, he's not telling you. It's a sealed deal if he owns a gimbal he bought on Tap.az and has used eleven times.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 every SMM in Baku just felt this.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #4
body: Ask about payment. Not the amount, the timing. Baku clients pay late, this is universal, and every marketing person has one story about a business owner who ghosted after three months of work. He now takes 50 percent upfront and says so in the first meeting, and he learned that the expensive way. It's a sealed deal if there is a specific salon in this city that he will not name but whose owner he would recognise across a room.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 every SMM in Baku just felt this.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #5
body: Listen for the vocabulary. Reach, engagement, target, kontent, kreativ, all pronounced in Azerbaijani, none translated, all delivered to a client who does not know what any of them mean and nods anyway. He knows the client doesn't know. The client knows he knows. The meeting proceeds regardless. It's a sealed deal if he has ever sent a report that nobody opened and got paid for it anyway.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 every SMM in Baku just felt this.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #6
body: Ask about the influencers. Every campaign in Baku eventually becomes a negotiation with a blogger who wants more than the entire production budget, and he has done this negotiation forty times. He knows all their rates. He knows which ones actually convert and which ones have an audience in another country. He will not tell you which is which. It's a sealed deal if he has a note on his phone ranking Baku bloggers by whether they reply.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 every SMM in Baku just felt this.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku SMM Person. Tip #7
body: Watch what happens at 11pm. That's when the editing starts, because the day was meetings and shooting and the client wanted three changes. He will tell you he's fixing his sleep schedule. He has been fixing his sleep schedule since 2022. It's a sealed deal if he has ever exported a video, watched it once, found one frame wrong, and re-exported the entire thing at 2am.
